title: Can a 'Typing Error' Take Away Your Pay Scale?
desc: The Supreme Court held in 2026 that a university cannot deny a professor his advertised pay scale by calling it a typing error years later.
why: The Supreme Court recently set aside a 2024 Uttarakhand High Court order that let a university withhold a professor's higher pay scale by calling it an advertisement typo, a question many government employees in Uttarakhand face.
keyPoints: The Supreme Court held in 2026 that a university cannot deny an employee his advertised pay scale by calling it a typing error.
Dr. Harish Chandra Tiwari was appointed in 2016 on a lower scale, though his post's regulations fixed a higher one.
The Uttarakhand High Court had dismissed his case in 2024, accepting the university's 'typographical error' argument.
The university must now work out and pay his arrears from his 2016 joining date.

sections.h: Can a government employer deny a pay scale by calling it a mistake?
p: No, not if a rule or regulation already fixed that pay scale for the post. The Supreme Court held in 2026 that Uttarakhand Sanskrit University could not deny Dr. Harish Chandra Tiwari the Rs. 37,400-67,000 pay band advertised for his Associate Professor post in 2015, simply by calling it a typographical error.

The university had appointed him in 2016 on the lower Rs. 15,600-39,100 scale, and the Uttarakhand High Court dismissed his writ petition in 2024, accepting that the advertisement contained a clerical mistake. The Supreme Court disagreed and set that order aside.

sections.h: Why does this matter for government staff in Uttarakhand?
p: The reasoning applies beyond one professor. If a university or government rule already fixes the pay scale for a post, under University Grants Commission (UGC) norms or a state pay order, an employer cannot later deny that scale just by saying the advertisement or appointment letter was wrong.

The Court also noted that other staff in similarly placed posts had already received the benefit, so refusing it to one employee was unfair. This principle can matter to teachers, lecturers and other state employees across Uttarakhand pursuing pay fixation or arrears claims.

whatToDo: Keep your original advertisement, appointment letter and any pay-fixation or government orders for your post — the advertisement often shows the scale the post was meant to carry.
Check whether a service rule, UGC regulation or pay commission order fixes your post's scale; that can override a later claim of 'clerical error'.
Raise the issue first through a written representation to your department before approaching a tribunal or court.
Take legal advice on your own facts, since the right forum (Central Administrative Tribunal, civil court or High Court) depends on your type of post.

hi.title: क्या सरकारी नौकरी में वेतनमान को 'टाइपिंग एरर' बताकर रोका जा सकता है?
keyPoints: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 2026 में कहा कि विश्वविद्यालय किसी कर्मचारी को विज्ञापन में दिया गया वेतनमान 'टाइपिंग एरर' बताकर नहीं रोक सकता।
डॉ. हरीश चंद्र तिवारी को 2016 में कम वेतनमान पर नियुक्त किया गया था, जबकि नियमों के तहत पद का वेतनमान अधिक था।
उत्तराखंड हाईकोर्ट ने 2024 में यह याचिका खारिज कर दी थी, विश्वविद्यालय की 'टाइपिंग एरर' वाली दलील मानते हुए।
अब विश्वविद्यालय को 2016 से बकाया राशि की गणना कर भुगतान करना होगा।
p: अगर कोई नियम या सरकारी आदेश पहले से किसी पद का वेतनमान तय कर चुका है, तो उसे बाद में 'गलती' बताकर रोका नहीं जा सकता। उत्तराखंड के सरकारी कर्मचारी अपने वेतन या बकाया राशि से जुड़े मामलों में इस सिद्धांत का हवाला दे सकते हैं।

sources.title: Dr. Harish Chandra Tiwari vs Union of India, Uttarakhand High Court, WP No. 67/2021(S/B), judgment dated 05.07.2024 (Indian Kanoon)
Supreme Court sets aside High Court order in Dr. Harish Chandra Tiwari's pay scale case (SupremeToday)
